159.title: House Republicans' Extreme Demands will Set the Country on a Dangerous Path | Democrats Will Vote No
159.description:
House Republicans’ extreme Interior funding bill is a far-right wish list, slashing EPA funds by nearly 40% and gutting the National Park Service by almost half a billion…

Their demands will set our country on a dangerous path.

This bill will:
• Gut the National Park Service by almost half a billion, reducing our rangers’ ability to protect our special places.

• ZERO OUT ALL funding for environmental justice, denying communities the opportunity to protect themselves from environmental & health hazards.

• Slash the @EPA’s budget by nearly 40%, jeopardizing communities’ clean air + water to gain favor with industry

• Remove Endangered Species Act protections from cherished, vulnerable species across the country, from the gray wolf to the Northern long-eared bat.

• Slow down environmental reviews (aren’t they always complaining how slow they are?)

• Sell out our public lands and waters to toxic mining operations and fossil fuel projects.

From top to bottom, this bill will endanger all the American values and symbols we hold dear, from our national parks to vulnerable wildlife to our clean air and water.

167.title: Virtual Roundtable on the Indian Child Welfare Act
167.description:
On Tuesday, May 9 at 11:00 a.m. Eastern, House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Raúl M. Grijalva (D-Ariz.) held a virtual roundtable to discuss the history and significance of the Indian Child Welfare Act (ICWA). ICWA is a more than 40-year-old law that protects the well-being and best interests of Native children and families in state child welfare systems. In the past several years, ICWA has faced a series of legal challenges, the most prominent being the Brackeen v. Haaland Supreme Court case.

The virtual roundtable will feature expert panelists to discuss the history of ICWA and the role Congress can play to strengthen ICWA and protect Native children and families. This is the first congressional convening to examine ICWA since the onset of recent litigation efforts. 

– Panelists –
Mr. Jack Trope
Senior Director for Indian Child Welfare Programs
Casey Family Programs
Seattle, WA

Ms. Veronica Krupnick 
Foster Youth Advocacy Programs Coordinator 
CASA First
Santa Fe, NM

Hon. Karen Returns to War
Co-Chair
Northern Arapaho Business Council
Ft. Washakie, WY

Ms. Maggie Blackhawk
Professor of Law
NYU School of Law
New York, NY

* This video has been re-uploaded to fix audio issues at the beginning of the event. The original livestream with the audio issues remains accessible; please reach out if you require access.

173.title: Press Conference - Baaj Nwaavjo I’tah Kukveni Grand Canyon National Monument Designation Effort
173.description: During a virtual press conference held April 11 at 10:30am AZ/1:30pm ET, members of the Grand Canyon Tribal Coalition, joined by House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Raúl M. Grijalva (D-Ariz.) and Senator Kyrsten Sinema (I-Ariz.), launched an effort to call on President Joe Biden to use his authorities under the Antiquities Act of 1906 to designate the Baaj Nwaavjo I’tah Kukveni Grand Canyon National Monument. Baaj Nwaavjo means “where tribes roam” for the Havasupai Tribe and I’tah Kukveni means “our footprints” for the Hopi Tribe.

180.title: Hybrid FC Markup 9.21.2022
180.description:
On Wednesday, September 21, 2022, at 10:00 a.m. ET in 1324 Longworth Hearing Room and via Webex, and livestreamed on the Committee’s YouTube page, the Committee on Natural Resources will meet to consider the following bill and the following postponed recorded votes that were requested at the Committee’s most recent business meeting: 

H.R. 4690 (Rep. Jared Huffman), To reauthorize and amend the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act, and for other purposes. “Sustaining America’s Fisheries for the Future Act of 2021.” 
Postponed recorded votes requested at the Committee’s most recent business meeting:

Adopting as amended and ordering reported unfavorably: H.Res. 1247 (Rep. Garret Graves), Of inquiry directing the Secretary of the Interior to transmit certain documents to the House of Representatives relating to the 2023–2028 five-year program for offshore oil and gas leasing.
Adopting as amended and ordering reported unfavorably: H.Res. 1248 (Rep. Yvette Herrell), Of inquiry directing the Secretary of the Interior to transmit certain documents to the House of Representatives relating to the compliance with the obligations of the Mineral Leasing Act.
Adopting as amended and ordering reported unfavorably: H.Res. 1251 (Rep. Pete Stauber), Of inquiry directing the Secretary of Agriculture to transmit certain documents to the House of Representatives relating to the mineral withdrawal within the Superior National Forest.
Adopting as amended and ordering reported unfavorably: H.Res. 1252 (Rep. Pete Stauber), Of inquiry directing the Secretary of the Interior to transmit certain documents to the House of Representatives relating to the mineral withdrawal within the Superior National Forest.  
Adopting as amended and ordering reported unfavorably: H.Res. 1253 (Ranking Member Bruce Westerman), Of inquiry directing the Secretary of the Interior to transmit certain documents to the House of Representatives relating to the actions of the Department of the Interior’s Departmental Ethics Office.
Measure text and amendments can also be found by visiting the U.S. House of Representatives Committee Repository, found here.

185.title: Hybrid SCIP Legislative Hearing – September 14, 2022
185.description:
On Wednesday, September 14, 2022 at 1:00 p.m. ET, in room 1324 Longworth House Office Building and via Cisco WebEx, the Subcommittee for Indigenous Peoples of the United States (SCIP) will hold a hybrid legislative hearing on the following bills:  

H.R. 6032 (Rep. Jared Huffman, D-CA), To take certain Federal lands located in Siskiyou County, California, and Humboldt County, California, into trust for the benefit of the Karuk Tribe, and for other purposes. Katimiîn and Ameekyáaraam Sacred Lands Act.
H.R. 6964 (Rep. Marilyn Strickland, D-WA), To authorize leases of up to 99 years for lands held in trust for the Confederated Tribes of the Chehalis Reservation.
H.R. 7581 [Discussion Draft ANS to H.R. 7581 - attached] (Rep. Jared Huffman, D-CA), To recognize tribal cooperation in the environmental review of proposed actions affecting the revised Yurok Reservation, and for other purposes. Yurok Lands Act of 2022.
H.R. 8115 (Rep. Doug LaMalfa, R-CA), To amend the Recreation and Public Purposes Act to authorize sales and leases of certain Federal land to federally recognized Indian Tribes, and for other purposes. Recreation and Public Purposes Tribal Parity Act.
H.R. 8286 (Rep. Derek Kilmer, D-WA), To take certain Federal land in the State of Washington into trust for the Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe, and for other purposes.
H.R. 8380 (Rep. Jesús G. “Chuy” García, D-IL), To provide for the settlement of claims relating to the Shab-eh-nay Band Reservation in Illinois, and for other purposes. Prairie Band Potawatomi Nation Shab-eh-nay Band Reservation Settlement Act of 2022.
H.R. 8387 (Rep. Dan Newhouse, R-WA), To amend the Indian Law Enforcement Reform Act to provide for advancements in public safety services to Indian communities, and for other purposes. Parity for Tribal Law Enforcement Act.
This hearing will be streamed on YouTube. For hearing materials and schedules, please visit U.S. House of Representatives, Committee Repository at http://docs.house.gov/.

196.title: Hybrid Full Committee Markup July 13, 2022
196.description:
On Wednesday, July 13, 2022, at 10:00 a.m. ET in 1324 Longworth Hearing Room, via Webex, and livestreamed on the Committee’s YouTube page, the Committee on Natural Resources will meet to consider the following bills: 

H.R. 2794 (Rep. Betty McCollum), To provide for the protection of the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness and interconnected Federal lands and waters, including Voyageurs National Park, within the Rainy River Watershed in the State of Minnesota, and for other purposes. Boundary Waters Wilderness Protection and Pollution Prevention Act.  
H.R. 3686 (Rep. Ann M. Kuster), To amend the Omnibus Parks and Public Lands Management Act of 1996 to provide for the establishment of a Ski Area Fee Retention Account, and for other purposes. SHRED Act or Ski Hill Resources for Economic Development Act. 
H.R. 5715 (Rep. Raúl M. Grijalva), To reauthorize the Morris K. Udall and Stewart L. Udall Trust Fund, and for other purposes. 
H.R. 6364 (Rep. Matt Cartwright), To amend the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area Improvement Act to extend the exception to the closure of certain roads within the Recreation Area for local businesses, and for other purposes. 
H.R. 6442 (Rep. Russ Fulcher), To amend section 101703 of title 54, United States Code, to include Tribal Governments and quasi-governmental entities, and for other purposes. PACTS Act or Partnership Agreements Creating Tangible Savings Act.
H.R. 6654 (Rep. Raúl M. Grijalva), To direct the Secretary of the Interior to establish a National Climate Adaptation Science Center and Regional Climate Adaptation Science Centers to respond to the effects of extreme weather events and climate trends, and for other purposes. CASC Act or Climate Adaptation Science Centers Act. 
H.R. 6936 (Rep. Elise Stefanik), To provide for the issuance of a semipostal to benefit programs that combat invasive species. Stamp Out Invasive Species Act.
H.R. 7283 (Rep. Matt Cartwright), To amend the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act to make certain activities eligible for grants from the Abandoned Mine Reclamation Fund, and for other purposes.STREAM Act or Safeguarding Treatment for the Restoration of Ecosystems from Abandoned Mines Act.
H.R. 7496 (Rep. Stacey E. Plaskett), To direct the Secretary of the Interior to install a plaque at the peak of Ram Head in the Virgin Islands National Park on St. John, United States Virgin Islands, to commemorate the slave rebellion that began on St. John in 1733.
H.R. 7693 (Rep. Bruce Westerman), To amend title 54, United States Code, to reauthorize the National Park Foundation. National Park Foundation Reauthorization Act of 2022.
Bill texts and amendments in the nature of a substitute can also be found by visiting the U.S. House of Representatives Committee Repository, found here.

198.description:
On Thursday, June 23, 2022 at 10:00 a.m. ET, in room 1324 Longworth House Office Building and via Cisco WebEx the Subcommittee on National Parks, Forests, and Public Lands will hold a hybrid legislative hearing on the following bills:



H.R. 2522 (Rep. Teresa Leger Fernandez, D-NM) To amend the John D. Dingell, Jr. Conservation, Management, and Recreation Act to establish the Cerro de la Olla Wilderness in the Río Grande del Norte National Monument and to modify the boundary of the Río Grande del Norte National Monument. H.R. 2882 (Rep. Steven Horsford, D-NV) To extend the authorization of the Mormon Pioneer National Heritage Area, to designate the Great Basin National Heritage Route in the State of Nevada as the “Great Basin National Heritage Area”, to designate the Great Basin Heritage Route Partnership as the “Great Basin Heritage Area Partnership”, to extend the authorization of the Great Basin National Heritage Area, and for other purposes. Great Basin National Heritage Area and Mormon Pioneer National Heritage Area Extension Act.
H.R. 5355 (Rep. Jay Obernolte, R-CA) To convey certain Federal land in California to Apple Valley, California, Twentynine Palms, California, Barstow, California, and Victorville, California. Desert Community Lands Act.
H.R. 6240 (Rep. Chris Stewart, R-UT) To release the reversionary interest of the United States in certain non-Federal land in Salt Lake City, Utah, and for other purposes.
H.R. 7509 (Rep. Peter DeFazio, D-OR) To expand certain land administered by the Bureau of Land Management and Forest Service in the State of Oregon as wilderness and a national recreation area, and for other purposes. Wild Rogue Conservation and Recreation Enhancement Act.

H.R. 7792 (Rep. Melanie Stansbury, D-NM) To provide for a national water data framework, and for other purposes. Water Data Act.

201.title: NPFPL Legislative Hearing – June 14, 2022
201.description:
On Tuesday, June 14, 2022 at 10:00 a.m. ET, in room 1324 Longworth House Office Building and via Cisco WebEx the Subcommittee on National Parks, Forests, and Public Lands will hold a hybrid legislative hearing on the following bills:

H.R. 1548 (Rep. Matt Cartwright, D-PA) To establish a pilot program for native plant species, and for other purposes. Native Plant Species Pilot Program Act of 2021. 
H.R. 4658 (Rep. Ted Lieu, D-CA) To designate the Encinal Trailhead on the Backbone Trail in the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area as the “Anthony ‘Tony’ Beilenson Trailhead.” Beilenson Trailhead Designation Act.
H.R. 6364 (Rep. Matt Cartwright, D-PA) To amend the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area Improvement Act to extend the exception to the closure of certain roads within the Recreation Area for local businesses, and for other purposes.
H.R. 6442 (Rep. Russ Fulcher, R-ID) To amend section 101703 of title 54, United States Code, to include Tribal Governments and quasi-governmental entities, and for other purposes. PACTS Act. 
H.R. 7496 (Rep. Stacey Plaskett, D-VI) To direct the Secretary of the Interior to install a plaque at the peak of Ram Head in the Virgin Islands National Park on St. John, United States Virgin Islands, to commemorate the slave rebellion that began on St. John in 1733. 
H.R. 7615 (Rep. Blake Moore, R-UT) To authorize the Secretary of the Interior to enter into partnerships to develop housing, and for other purposes. LODGE Act. 
H.R. 7693 (Rep. Bruce Westerman, R-AR) To amend title 54, United States Code, to reauthorize the National Park Foundation. National Park Foundation Reauthorization Act of 2022. 
H.R. 7952 (Rep. Madeleine Dean, D-PA) To authorize the Secretary of the Interior to issue a right-of-way permit with respect to a natural gas distribution pipeline within Valley Forge National Historical Park, and for other purposes. Valley Forge Park Realignment Permit and Promise Act.

204.title: Public Input Forum on Puerto Rico Status Act Discussion Draft
204.description:
House Committee on Natural Resources Chair Raúl M. Grijalva will hold a public input forum on the Puerto Rico Status Act discussion draft to seek input from members of the public on Saturday, June 4 from 3 to 8:30 PM Eastern at the Puerto Rico Convention Center in San Juan.

Members of the public who wish to attend and view the proceedings can register at https://prstatusforum.eventbrite.com.

Interested stakeholders and members of the public are encouraged to share your views on the legislation via the online public input platform at https://www.popvox.com/us/federal/prop/117/3. Comments will be shared with Members of the House Natural Resources Committee and included in the congressional record.

211.title: NPFPL Legislative Hearing – May 11, 2022

On Wednesday, May 11, 2022 at 2:00 p.m. (ET), in room 1324 Longworth House Office Building and via Cisco WebEx the Subcommittee on National Parks, Forests, and Public Lands will hold a hybrid legislative hearing on the following bills:

H.R. 279 (Rep. Ruben Gallego, D-AZ) To provide lasting protection for inventoried roadless areas within the National Forest System. Roadless Area Conservation Act of 2021. 
H.R. 7329 (Rep. Jared Huffman, D-CA) To amend the Smith River National Recreation Area Act to include certain additions to the Smith River National Recreation Area, to amend the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act to designate certain wild rivers in the State of Oregon, and for other purposes. Smith River National Recreation Area Expansion Act.
H.R. 7399 (Rep. James Comer, R-KY) To amend the Land Between the Lakes Protection Act of 1998 to clarify the administration of the Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area, and for other purposes. LBL Recreation and Heritage Act. 
H.R. XXXX (Rep. Earl Blumenauer, D-OR) To provide for conservation and recreation enhancement for Mount Hood and the Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area, and for other purposes. Mt. Hood and Columbia River Gorge Recreation Enhancement and Conservation (REC) Act of 2022.
This hearing will be streamed on YouTube. For hearing materials and schedules, please visit U.S. House of Representatives, Committee Repository at http://docs.house.gov/.

On Wednesday, April 27, 2022 at 1:00 p.m. ET, in room 1324 Longworth House Office Building (Hearing Room) and online via Cisco Webex, the Subcommittee for Indigenous Peoples of the United States (SCIP) will host a hybrid legislative hearing on the following tribal-related legislation:

H.R. 437 (Rep. Don Young, R-AK), To amend the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act to exclude certain payments to Alaska Native elders for determining eligibility for certain programs, and for other purposes.
H.R. 6063 (Rep. Betty McCollum, D-MN), To provide for the equitable settlement of certain Indian land disputes regarding land in Illinois, and for other purposes.
H.R. 6181 [Discussion Draft ANS to H.R. 6181 - attached] (Rep. Ruben Gallego, D-AZ), To reaffirm that certain land has been taken into trust for the benefit of the Samish Indian Nation, and for other purposes. “Samish Indian Nation Land Reaffirmation Act.”
S. 314 (Sen. Jeff Merkley, D-OR), To repeal the Klamath Tribe Judgment Fund Act. “Klamath Tribe Judgment Fund Repeal Act.”
S. 559 (Sen. Jeff Merkley, D-OR), To amend the Grand Ronde Reservation Act, and for other purposes.
S. 789 (Sen. Mike Rounds, R-SD), To repeal certain obsolete laws relating to Indians. “Repealing Existing Substandard Provisions Encouraging Conciliation with Tribes Act.”

H.R. 6785 (Rep. Seth Moulton, D-MA) To assist in the conservation of the North Atlantic right whale by supporting and providing financial resources for North Atlantic right whale conservation programs and projects of persons with expertise required for the conservation of North Atlantic right whales, and for other purposes. Right Whale Coexistence Act of 2022.
H.R. 6987 (Rep. Rick Larsen, D-WA) [Introduced text attached] To establish programs to reduce the impacts of vessel traffic and underwater noise on marine mammals, and for other purposes.

229.title: Full Committee Markup 2.16.22
229.description:
On Wednesday, February 16, 2022, at 10:00 a.m. EST, the Committee on Natural Resources will meet to consider the following measures: 

H.R. 1546 (Rep. Carter of Georgia), To amend the Eliminate, Neutralize, and Disrupt Wildlife Trafficking Act of 2016 to direct the Presidential Task Force on Wildlife Trafficking to develop recommendations to address wildlife trafficking on the internet and on social media, and to direct the Secretary of State and the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development to develop a strategy to address wildlife trafficking on the internet and on social media, and for other purposes. Combating Online Wildlife Trafficking Act of 2021.
H.R. 3525 (Rep. Meng), To establish the Commission to Study the Potential Creation of a National Museum of Asian Pacific American History and Culture, and for other purposes. Commission To Study the Potential Creation of a National Museum of Asian Pacific American History and Culture Act.
H.R. 3540 (Rep. Sarbanes), To reauthorize the Chesapeake Bay Office of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and for other purposes. Chesapeake Bay Science, Education, and Ecosystem Enhancement Act of 2021.
H.R. 4458 (Rep. Huffman), To establish a grant program within the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration to award grants to eligible entities for the purpose of carrying out projects on the conservation, restoration, or management of kelp forest ecosystems. KELP Act. 
H.R. 4677 (Rep. Tonko), To direct restoration and protection of the New York-New Jersey watersheds and estuaries hydrologically connected to New York-New Jersey Harbor, and for other purposes. New York-New Jersey Watershed Protection Act.
H.R. 5973 (Rep. Dingell), To reauthorize the Great Lakes Fish and Wildlife Restoration Act of 1990, and for other purposes. Great Lakes Fish and Wildlife Restoration Reauthorization Act of 2021.
H.R. 6023 (Rep. Costa), To require the United States Postal Service to continue selling the Multinational Species Conservation Funds Semipostal Stamp until all remaining stamps are sold, and for other purposes. Multinational Species Conservation Funds Semipostal Stamp Reauthorization Act of 2021.
H.R. 6142 (Rep. Ryan), To amend the National Trails System Act to direct the Secretary of the Interior to conduct a study on the feasibility of designating the Buckeye Trail as a national scenic trail, and for other purposes. Buckeye National Scenic Trail Feasibility Study Act of 2021.
HR 6199 (Rep. Smith of Missouri), To revise the boundary of the Ste. Genevieve National Historical Park in the State of Missouri, and for other purposes. Ste. Genevieve National Historical Park Boundary Revision Act.
H.R. 6201 (Rep. Watson Coleman), To extend the authority for the establishment of a commemorative work to honor enslaved and free Black persons who served in the American Revolution, and for other purposes. National Liberty Memorial Preservation Act.
H.R. 6337 (Rep. Neguse), To require the Secretary of the Interior and the Secretary of Agriculture to develop long-distance bike trails on Federal land, and for other purposes. Biking on Long-Distance Trails Act.
H.R. 6434 (Rep. Obernolte), To direct the Secretary of the Interior to establish, within the National Park Service, the Japanese American World War II History Network, and for other purposes. Japanese American World War II History Network Act.
H.R. 6435 (Rep. McMorris Rodgers), To provide for the application of certain provisions of the Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Act of 2000 for fiscal year 2021.
H. Res. 641 (Rep. Newhouse), Recognizing and celebrating the 75th anniversary of the National Association of Conservation Districts and their commitment to our lands.

238.title: What More Public Lands Leasing Means for Achieving U.S. Climate Targets
238.description: Fossil fuel extraction from America’s #PublicLands and waters makes our #ClimateCrisis worse. A quarter of U.S. greenhouse gas emissions come from leases on public lands, and cutting those emissions is a big part of our climate solution. But the Bureau of Land Management is advancing new oil and gas lease sales on public lands early next year, making it harder to stop the #ClimateCrisis. Join us for our Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee oversight hearing on Thursday, December 2, on cutting emissions and protecting people and the environment. Watch live here at 10 a.m. Eastern.

245.title: Wildland Firefighting Workforce Reforms
245.description: We need to pay firefighters protecting our homes and public lands what they deserve. As we all know, #ClimateChange is a major driver of our increasingly intense wildfires, making fire season months longer than in the past. Wildfires are now a nearly year-round threat in some areas. Over the last 30 years the land affected by wildfires in the Western U.S. has doubled, and it’s only getting worse. On Wednesday, October 27, we’re hosting a legislative hearing on supporting and protecting firefighters who battle intense fires and protect our communities. Watch live here at 10 a.m. Eastern time.

248.title: Runit Dome and the U.S Nuclear Legacy in the Marshall Islands
248.description:
On Thursday, October 21, the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations, led by Chair Katie Porter (D-Calif.), will hold an oversight hearing titled, Runit Dome and the U.S Nuclear Legacy in the Marshall Islands. 

In April 1947, the U.S. entered into an agreement with the United Nations Security Council to administer the Marshall Islands as a Trust Territory. Under this agreement, the U.S. retained the right to use the Marshall Islands for military tests. From 1946 to 1958, the U.S. conducted 67 nuclear weapons tests in the Marshall Islands, exposing the islands and its residents to unprecedented amounts of radiation. In 1977, nuclear waste and debris was placed in a storage facility called Runit Dome.

The U.S. has never apologized to the Marshallese for the nuclear testing and continues to evade responsibility for providing monetary compensation, administering adequate health care, and conducting environmental monitoring of Runit Dome. The U.S. has a moral responsibility and a national security imperative to negotiate in good faith with the Republic of the Marshall Islands over the legacy of U.S. nuclear testing in the islands.

Watch live here at 10 a.m. Eastern.

249.title: Colorado River Drought Conditions and Response Measures – Day Two
249.description:
On Wednesday, October 20, the Subcommittee on Water, Oceans, and Wildlife, led by Chair Jared Huffman (D-Calif.), will hold an oversight hearing titled, Colorado River Drought Conditions and Response Measures – Day Two. This will be the second session of a two-part hearing. The recording of the first session, which was held Friday, Oct. 15 at 2:00 p.m. Eastern time is available to view here: https://naturalresources.house.gov/hearings/colorado-river-drought-conditions-and-response-measures_day-one 

Climate change and severe drought in the Colorado River Basin threaten water supplies for 40 million people in the Southwest. The Colorado River Drought Contingency Plan authorized by Congress in 2019 is helping mitigate some drought impacts until its expiration in 2026, but additional response measures are needed to strengthen climate resilience for communities across the Southwest.

Watch live here at 11 a.m. Eastern.

252.title: Impacts of Abandoned Offshore Oil and Gas Infrastructure and the Need for Stronger Federal Oversight
252.description: The ongoing oil spill on the coast of California is a major environmental disaster - and a firsthand look at the dangers proposed by aging oil and gas infrastructure. Our coasts are littered with thousands of abandoned pipelines that threaten communities, wildlife, the environment and taxpayers. On Thursday, October 14, the Subcommittee on Energy and Mineral Resources will host an oversight hearing on the need for stronger federal oversight over offshore oil and gas infrastructure. It’s time to take action against polluters that shift cleanup costs to taxpayers at the community’s expense. Watch live here at 12 p.m. Eastern.

255.title: PREPA Post Implementation of the LUMA Transmission and Distribution Contract
255.description: On Wednesday, October 6, the Committee on Natural Resources Office of Insular Affairs will host a full committee oversight hearing titled “PREPA Post Implementation of the LUMA Transmission and Distribution Contract.” LUMA Energy took over management of Puerto Rico’s electric grid in June of this year, but the transition has not gone smoothly. Power outages and other disruptions continue to harm Puerto Ricans. We’re investigating this transition to ensure Puerto Rico is prioritizing a renewable future that meets everyone’s needs. Watch live here at 1 p.m. Eastern time.

270.title: Remote WOW Legislative Hearing – June 29, 2021
270.description: Receding water levels at the Salton Sea are spreading toxic dust with dangerous levels of selenium, arsenic and industrial runoff. This hurts air quality and destroys habitats for endangered species and water birds. We’re holding a Water, Oceans, and Wildlife Subcommittee legislative hearing on Tuesday, June 29, on bills to address this and other water quality and water access issues. We’ll discuss increasing funding to address environmental impacts at the Salton Sea and bills to address and prepare for drought across the West. Watch live here at 1:00 p.m. Eastern time.

273.title: Examining Federal Facilities in Indian Country
273.description: Many federal facilities in Indian Country are falling apart and failing their communities because of decades of congressional underfunding. Until these infrastructure concerns are fully addressed, tribal communities will keep suffering from relatively poor education, health care and public safety services. We’re hosting a Subcommittee for Indigenous Peoples of the United States oversight hearing on Thursday, June 17, examining how the American Jobs Plan represents a new opportunity to invest in Indian Country. Watch live here at 12:00 p.m. Eastern.

278.title: Environmental Justice for Coal Country: Supporting Communities Through the Energy Transition
278.description: Rural and tribal coal mining communities are on the front lines of our nation’s ongoing energy transition. Bankrupt coal companies are leaving behind pollution and economic devastation, and unless Congress puts strong financial standards in place, this will all have to be cleaned up with public money. We can ensure a #JustTransition focused on #EnviroJusticeNow with a more sustainable and equitable energy future for coal communities across the country. We’re hosting an Energy and Mineral Resources oversight hearing on Tuesday. June 15, to investigate how the Office of Surface Mining Reclamation and Enforcement can help coal communities #BuildBackBetter. Watch live here at 10:00 a.m. Eastern.

279.title: DDT Dumping Off the Southern California Coast: Ecological Impacts, Scientific Needs, and Next Steps
279.description: DDT barrels were dumped in federal waters off the shore of Southern California regularly until 1970. Since then, scientists have recorded dangerously high levels of the chemical in marine wildlife. Congress banned ocean dumping decades ago, but no law addresses the damage this dumping has already done. We’re hosting a Subcommittee on Water, Oceans, and Wildlife oversight hearing on Tuesday, June 8, to discus what additional steps might be necessary. Watch live here at 3:00 p.m. Eastern.

281.title: Introducing the Ocean-Based Climate Solutions Act
281.description: In honor of World Oceans Day, Chair Raúl M. Grijalva (D-Ariz.) today introduced the Ocean-Based Climate Solutions Act, an updated version of a bill he initially offered in the previous Congress to modernize federal ocean management policy to account for climate change. The bill limits climate impacts on marine habitats, promotes carbon sinks in federal waters, advances Arctic conservation efforts with climate change in mind, modernizes fishing fleet fuel regulations and takes other steps to align ocean policies with modern environmental and economic reality.

283.title: The Status of Drought Conditions Throughout the Western United States
283.description: The western United States are currently experiencing severe, climate change-related drought conditions, with 86 percent of the West categorized as being under some degree of drought. Severe water supply shortages are already impacting communities, ecosystems, and whole economies. On Tuesday, May 25, the Subcommittee on Water, Oceans, and Wildlife will discuss the necessity of, and best way to implement, short- and long-term solutions for the coming crisis. Watch live here at 1:00 p.m. Eastern.

286.title: Misuse of Taxpayer Dollars & Corporate Welfare in the Oil and Gas Industry

The fossil fuel industry keeps demanding government handouts and says environmental and health standards will kill jobs. How credible are they? How seriously should we take these claims of economic benefits from corporate welfare for oil and gas? Our Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations, led by Chair Katie Porter, is holding an oversight hearing on Wednesday, May 19. Watch live here at 1:00 p.m. Eastern.

We’re hosting a Energy and Mineral Resources Hearing on Thursday, May 13, to protect coastal communities from offshore drilling and fight for #OceanClimateAction. Watch live here at 1:00 p.m Eastern.

289.title: Full Committee Hearing - Insular Cases Resolution
289.description: The legal precedent created by a set of rulings known as the Insular Cases set up a “separate and unequal” doctrine for the residents of the five populated U.S. Territories. To this day, federal courts continue to use this as justification to deny territory residents fair taxation, access to federal programs, and even voting rights. On Wednesday, May 12, we’re hosting a legislative hearing on H.Res.279, which calls on the legal system to abandon this unfair set of standards. Watch live here at 1:00 p.m. Eastern.

292.title: WOW Legislative Hearing - Restoring Resilient Reefs Act
292.description: Coral reef ecosystems support about 25 percent of all marine life. Climate change, disease outbreaks and ecosystem loss have destroyed coral across the world and now threaten its very existence. On Tuesday, May 4, we’re hosting a Water, Oceans, and Wildlife legislative hearing on Rep. Darren Soto’s Restoring Resilient Reefs Act to give coral the protection it needs to survive. Watch live here at 3 p.m. Eastern time as we work to protect and restore our coral reefs with #OceanClimateAction.

295.title: Wildlife Trafficking and the Growing Online Marketplace

The illegal trade of wildlife and associated products threatens the survival of species across the planet. We’re hosting a Water, Oceans and Wildlife oversight subcommittee hearing on Tuesday, April 27, on regulating the wildlife trade and protecting species from trafficking and extinction. Watch live here at 3:00 p.m. Eastern.

297.title: NPFPL Legislative Hearing – April 21, 2021

298.title: Infrastructure in Indigenous Communities: Priorities for American Jobs Plan
298.description: Thanks to decades of federal neglect, many Native American communities lack broadband internet access, well-maintained roads, accessible utilities and adequate housing. It’s time to put them front and center in the next round of infrastructure investments. We’re hosting a Subcommittee for Indigenous Peoples of the United States hearing on infrastructure in Indigenous communities and how the American Jobs Plan can benefit Native families. Watch live here on Wednesday, April 21, at 10 a.m. as we assess how federal investments can best create jobs and improve infrastructure in Indian Country.

299.title: Building Back Better: Reducing Pollution and Creating Jobs Through Offshore Wind
299.description: The #ClimateCrisis demands a transition from fossil fuels to a clean energy economy. The Biden administration recently announced major support for and investment in offshore wind production. We’re stepping up to advance bills that create sustainable jobs, support the fast-growing wind power industry and strengthen federal support for clean energy in Congress. Watch our Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee’s live legislative hearing on Tuesday, April 20, here at 2:30 p.m. Eastern.

300.title: Building Back Better: Creating Jobs and Reducing Pollution by Plugging and Reclaiming Orphaned Wells
300.description: Communities suffer when oil and gas companies abandon their drilling sites and don’t clean them up. We know that oil and gas development has broad environmental impacts and public health impacts. It’s imperative that we do everything possible to limit the risk and damage done by this development. Wells abandoned by fossil fuel companies – known as orphaned wells – can create enormous environmental and health risks. They leak methane, contaminate our water and risk our safety. We’re hosting a hearing on Thursday, April 15 to review legislation to create a national strategy to plug these wells, create jobs and protect the environment. Watch live here at 2 p.m. Eastern.

303.title: How the Biden Administration’s Build Back Better Plan Can Benefit the U.S. Territories
303.description: U.S. territories and freely associated states have been hit by catastrophic natural disasters spurred by #ClimateChange. Hurricanes and typhoons have killed thousands of our fellow Americans and destroyed power plants, roads, ports, water and sewer systems, and public buildings. We’re hosting a hearing on Wednesday, March 24, to discuss infrastructure needs for territorial governments under the #BuildBackBetter plan. Watch live here at 10:00 a.m. Eastern.

305.title: Building Back Better: Examining the Future of America’s Public Lands
305.description: Protecting and managing #PublicLands will be key to fighting the #ClimateCrisis. Working with the Biden administration, we’re ready to follow the science and ensure that our public lands are part of the climate solution for the benefit of all Americans. We’re hosting a hearing in our National Parks, Forests and Public Lands Subcommittee with new Chair Rep. Joe Neguse on Tuesday, March 23, to ensure the economic and environmental potential of our public lands is part of our #BuildBackBetter plan. Watch live here at 10:00 a.m. Eastern.

306.title: Restoring Abandoned Mine Lands, Local Economies, and the Environment
306.description: Cleaning up abandoned mines protects public health and safety and creates jobs, especially in communities the mining industry has left behind. On Thursday, March 18, we’re hosting a hearing in the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee on three bills to restore abandoned mines, rebuild local economies and clean up the environment. Our plan will jump-start a cleaner economy and help communities take economic power back from polluters. Watch live here at 12 p.m. Eastern.

307.title: Vice Chair Haaland's Farewell Remarks on the House Floor
307.description:
Vice Chair Rep. Deb Haaland delivered farewell remarks to the House of Representatives on March 16, 2021.

Haaland is the new Secretary of the U.S. Department of the Interior. We’ll all benefit from her leadership of putting #PeopleOverPolluters, fighting the #ClimateCrisis, and advancing justice. We’re so grateful for her service to this Committee and the people it represents.

308.title: Building Back Better: Building Resilience for the Economy, Climate, and Ecosystems
308.description: The whole country is ready to build a resilient economy and prevent the worst impacts of climate change. Our #BuildBackBetter solutions mean more jobs, environmental justice for all, and working together in fighting the #ClimateCrisis. We’re hosting a hearing in our Water, Oceans and Wildlife Subcommittee led by Chair Jared Huffman on Thursday, March 11, to discuss solutions we can turn into law. Watch live here at 2 p.m. Eastern.

309.title: Modernizing Energy Development Laws for the Benefit of Taxpayers, Communities, and the Environment
309.description: Outdated laws and low royalties mean oil and gas companies have been paying a discounted rate to pollute our #PublicLands. It’s time for Congress to pass reforms that protect taxpayers, communities, the environment and our future. We’re hosting an Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee hearing led by Chair Alan Lowenthal on a package of bills that modernize our energy development laws on Tuesday, March 9. Watch live here at 12 p.m. Eastern.

310.title: Discussion on the Insular Area Climate Change Act
310.description: U.S.-affiliated Insular Areas like Puerto Rico are at the front lines of the #ClimateCrisis. The territories have faced major natural disasters because of #ClimateChange, including Hurricane Irma and Hurricane Maria in 2017 and Typhoon Yutu in 2018. On Thursday, March 4, we’ll receive feedback on Chair Grijalva’s discussion draft bill that provides climate change planning, mitigation, adaptation, and resilience in the U.S. Territories and Freely Associated States. Watch our Full Committee legislative hearing live here at 12 p.m. Eastern.

315.title: Environmental Justice Now Tour: Appalachia
315.description:
For decades the coal industry has wreaked havoc on the local culture, economy, health and environment of central Appalachia. Now, coal companies are going bankrupt, leaving behind pollution, health issues and economic uncertainty.
 
We’re hosting a virtual forum on Wednesday, December 9, to hear from community activists across Appalachia. Chair Raul M. Grijalva and Congressman Donald McEachin’s #EnviroJusticeNow legislation gives Appalachian communities they tools they need for a #JustTransition. Watch live here at 12 p.m. Eastern.

320.title: DIGITAL PRESS CONFERENCE: Ocean-Based Climate Solutions Act Rollout
320.description:
The oceans have absorbed 93 percent of heat trapped by the #ClimateCrisis, making them hotter and more acidic. We’ve got to #ActOnClimate, stop damage to our oceans, and protect the food, jobs & coastlines that people depend on.
 
Up to 21 percent of the annual greenhouse gas emissions cuts the world needs can come from the oceans. We’re introducing the country’s first comprehensive bill to address ocean climate solutions. It uses the oceans’ power to fight #ClimateChange and makes marine and coastal ecosystems and coastal communities more resilient to the changes we know are coming.
 
Watch our press conference on Oct. 20 at 1:30 p.m. Eastern time to learn more as we introduce this landmark legislation.

321.title: Environmental Justice for Coastal Communities: Examining Inequities in Federal Grantmaking
321.description: On October 15, our Subcommittee on Water, Oceans and Wildlife is hosting a remote oversight hearing to discuss the inequalities in federal grantmaking. The requirements for federal grants mean that often times underserved communities are left out of the application process – widening disparities and making it impossible to compete. It’s time to address these barriers on the Congressional level to ensure that #EnviroJusticeNow communities can prepare for the effects of #ClimateChange.

322.title: The Threat of Offshore Drilling and the Need for a Permanent Federal Ban
322.description:
The Trump administration proposed to lease more than 90% of America’s coastlines up to offshore oil and gas drilling.
 
In 2019, House Democrats passed #ProtectOurCoast bills that ban drilling on our coasts to protect the communities who live there. Trump opposes these bills and the Republican Senate refuses to act on them. We’re hosting a forum on Wednesday, October 14 to highlight the threat of offshore drilling and the need for a permanent federal ban. Watch live here at 2 p.m. Eastern.

We’re hosting a forum on Monday, October 5, to learn how the higher temperatures are wreaking havoc on wildlife, fisheries and humans who have call the Arctic home for generations. Watch live here at 2:00 p.m. Eastern time.

325.title: Legislative Hearing - Environmental Justice for All Act
325.description: Chair Raúl M. Grijalva and Rep. A. Donald McEachin have been researching, listening and working with the public for more than a year to put together the Environmental Justice for All Act. We’ve hosted an #EnvironmentalJustice tour to visit and hear from voices that are often left out of the conversation. Now we continue the fight for justice with a legislative hearing on our #EnviroJusticeNow bill on Thursday, October 1. Join us at 12:00 p.m. Eastern time as we discuss a bill the public helped write that really achieves environmental justice and restores civil rights.

328.title: Staff Led Colorado Environmental Justice Forum
328.description:
On Wednesday, September 16, at 12:00pm Eastern, Natural Resources committee staff hosted a briefing on environmental justice in the state of Colorado. While Colorado is considered a Mecca for outdoor enthusiasts, there is still rampant environmental injustices across the state. In the city of Denver, Globeville and Elyria-Swansea are some of oldest—and most polluted—neighborhoods in the city. With several nearby industrial factories, two busy interstate highways, diesel train traffic, and soil contamination from historical smelting operations, the communities of Globeville and Elyria-Swansea bear some of the nation’s highest environmental risk. Additionally, there are massive fracking activities, water and air quality issues in the State. 

PANELISTS 
• Colorado State Representative Dominque Jackson 
• Amy Gray- 350 Colorado 
• Eat Tafoya- Latino Forum 
• Jorge Figueroa- El Laboratorio

330.title: Federal and State Efforts to Restore the Salton Sea
330.description:
California's Salton Sea has been called "toxic," "post-apocalyptic," and "one of California’s most pressing ecological and environmental justice crises." The shrinking of the Salton Sea presents major health concerns for humans, endangered species and migratory birds.
 
As California implements Phase 1 of its Salton Sea management program, we’re hosting an oversight hearing in our Water, Oceans and Wildlife Subcommittee to discuss how we can best support management efforts and protect the environment. Join us and watch live on Thursday, September 24, at 12 p.m. Eastern time.

332.title: Trump Administration Broken Promises on Renewable Energy
332.description:
For four years, the Trump administration has provided nothing but lip service to renewable energy. The Department of Interior is pushing away opportunities to expand wind and solar energy programs and working overtime to hand our #PublicLands and waters over to fossil fuel companies for less money than a cup of coffee.
 
Promoting fossil fuels over renewable energy makes climate crisis even worse than it already is. This administration is  blocking opportunities to create new jobs, improve public health, and increase the nation’s security and competitiveness. We’re hosting an oversight hearing on Tuesday, September 22, to hold the Trump administration accountable and look at what it would mean to end this obstruction. Watch live here at 12 p.m. Eastern time.

333.title: Environmental Justice Now Tour: Los Angeles
333.description:
Los Angeles is the most polluted metropolitan area in the United States. Our Environmental Justice for All Act would mean cleaner, healthier lives for millions of Americans living there.
 
Within a 20-mile stretch, communities like Bell, Compton, Huntington Park, Lynwood, and South Gate are stuck between major highways, downtown Los Angeles, and the port of Long Beach. The population of this area is 98 percent people of color. Seventy-eight percent of households live below the federal poverty line.
 
Black and brown families are threatened by cumulative impacts from thousands of pollution sources -- groundwater threats, hazardous waste generators, solid waste sites and more.
 
Join us for the third event in our ongoing #EnviroJusticeNow tour on Friday, September 18, to hear from Los Angeles community leaders at 12 p.m. Eastern to hear how #EnviroJusticeNow can make the Los Angeles region – and the country – a cleaner, healthier, safer place to live.

335.title: Enviro Justice Now Tour: Louisiana Cancer Alley
335.description:
In a long stretch between New Orleans and Baton Rouge, predominantly Black communities in Cancer Alley have been forced to survive alongside more than 150 heavily polluting chemical plants and refineries. Families there have suffered from the cumulative impacts of fossil fuel pollution for decades - and our laws often ignore those cumulative impacts in making permitting decisions or sharing public health resources.
 
Chair Raul M. Grijalva and Congressman Donald A. McEachin’s #EnviroJusticeNow bill would fix this. Join us on Thursday, September 17, at 12:00 p.m. Eastern time as we hear from community leaders in Cancer Alley for the second event in our ongoing national #EnviroJusticeNow tour. 
 
Louisiana is still recovering from Hurricane Laura. Natural disasters are getting worse. We’re amplifying voices left out of the usual conversation about public health and how to protect vulnerable communities. Join us as we discuss how #EnvironmentalJustice plays a role in making live safer and healthier for American children, families and neighborhoods.
 
Our towns and cities didn’t choose to be dumping grounds. It’s time to give political and legal power back to the people to protect themselves.

337.title: William Pendley’s Unfitness to Lead the Bureau of Land Management
337.description:
President Trump put William Pendley in charge of the Bureau of Land Management, and now he oversees 10 percent of land in the United States. He’s anti-#PublicLands, anti-Indigenous, pro-polluter and anti-regulation. He moved BLM headquarters from Washington, D.C., to Grand Junction, Colo. with little explanation to staff, leading to long-time experts leaving the agency. He doesn’t believe in protecting the environment and he’s unfit for office. He’s held his position for more than a year and recently signed an order giving himself an extension even though the Republican Senate majority won’t hold a hearing on his record or vote to confirm him.
 
We’re hosting a livestream on Wednesday, September 9, at 12 p.m. Eastern time to hear from experts on the damage Pendley has done and the need to replace him. Join Chair Raúl M. Grijalva, Vice-Chair Deb Haaland and Rep. Jamie Raskin from the House Oversight and Reform Committee as we provide the accountability the Senate won’t.

338.description: On Tuesday, September 8, we’re continuing our #EnviroJusticeNow Tour and hearing virtually from panelists from New Mexico. 339.title: Environmental Justice Now Tour: Michigan
339.description:
The citizens of Michigan are suffering from the cumulative impacts of poverty, pollution, neglected infrastructure and climate change. Torrential rains recently destroyed two dams and created a state of emergency. More than 40,000 citizens from Midland were evacuated just before their homes were destroyed.
Flint and Detroit are still suffering from endless environmental injustices.
Chair Raul M. Grijalva and Congressman Donald McEachin are inviting frontline community members from across the state to speak on the challenges they face and how #EnviroJusticeNow can make their lives healthier and better. Tune in live at 3:30 p.m. Eastern time as we hear from activists and Flint community members on Thursday, July 30.

341.title: Unanswered Questions About the US Park Police's Attack on Peaceful Protesters
341.description:
On June 28, the Natural Resources Committee held an oversight hearing to investigate the violent June 1 attack by law enforcement agents against peaceful #BlackLivesMatter protesters at #LafayetteSquare near the White House. Acting U.S. Park Police Chief Gregory Monahan was invited to testify at that hearing, but refused.

We’re holding a second hearing on those attacks on Tuesday, July 28. Mr. Monahan will appear in person and answer our questions about why the assault happened, who issued the orders, why they issued those orders and how this event foreshadowed other violent police crackdowns around the country. We’ll also hear from Adam DeMarco, a West Point graduate, former Army officer and current major in the District of Columbia National Guard, who will appear under the Military Whistleblower Protection Act. We need to understand why this happened and who was responsible to keep Americans safe and see which policies need to be changed.

345.title: Monumental Decisions: A Long Overdue Reckoning with Racist Symbols on Our Public Lands
345.description:
Our Subcommittee on National Parks Forests, and Public Lands is hosting a legislative hearing on Tuesday, July 21, on bills to remove commemorative Confederate works from our federally funded #PublicLands and monuments. The way we present our history should be honest, inclusive and representative of ALL Americans. Protected historic sites play a critical role in the telling of our nation’s history. They shouldn’t glorify or commercialize violent insurrection against the United States or promote symbols of hate and bigotry.
Watch live here at 10 a.m. Eastern time.

346.title: Native Youth Perspectives on Mental Health and Healing
346.description: American Indian/Alaska Native youth between the ages of 15 and 24 are the most at-risk population in the United States. They face serious disparities in physical and mental health, education, and juvenile justice treatment. Combined with the coronavirus pandemic, these disparities have created a huge public health crisis for tribal communities. On Thursday, July 16, at 3 p.m. Eastern time, our Subcommittee for Indigenous Peoples of the United States will host a hearing on Native youth perspectives on mental health and healing.

352.title: The U.S. Park Police Attack on Peaceful Protesters at Lafayette Square
352.description:
We’re hosting an oversight hearing on Monday, June 29, to investigate law enforcement’s violent June 1 crackdown against peaceful protesters and accredited journalists at Lafayette Square in Washington, D.C. This will be the first formal congressional inquiry into the incident. 

We will focus on the Trump administration’s inadequate and changing explanation for the excessive use of force by U.S. Park Police and other agencies, and seek information on what Congress needs to do to make sure it isn’t repeated.

We’ll hear from a #BlackLivesMatter protester injured in the crackdown, a journalist attacked by police, and the Right Rev. Mariann Budde, bishop of the Episcopal Diocese of Washington, whose church Trump famously posed at for his photo op. Join us live here at 12 p.m. Eastern time.

We will focus on the Trump administration’s inadequate and changing explanation for the excessive use of force by U.S. Park Police and other agencies, and seek information on what Congress needs to do to make sure it isn’t repeated.

We’ll hear from a #BlackLivesMatter protester injured in the crackdown, a journalist attacked by police, and the Right Rev. Mariann Budde, bishop of the Episcopal Diocese of Washington, whose church Trump famously posed at for his photo op. Join us live here at 12 p.m. Eastern time.
snippet.channelTitle: House Natural Resources Committee Democrats

357.title: After Coronavirus: Building a Prosperous, Environmentally Friendly Economy
357.description: It’s estimated the #coronavirus pandemic will shrink our economy by $8 trillion. Our economic stimulus plan should put Americans back to work and address #ClimateChange at the same time. Rebuilding has to mean a sustainable economy for the future, not just temporary employment programs. We’re hosting a livestreamed online forum on Tuesday, June 9, at 2:30 p.m. Eastern time to discuss the transition to a pro-jobs, pro-environment economy.

359.title: Reclaiming Orphaned Oil and Gas Wells
359.description: There are almost 60,000 abandoned oil and gas rigs in America contaminating our water, polluting our air and not creating jobs. It’s time they get cleaned up. #Coronavirus has hit working Americans in the energy sector hard lately, and we have an opportunity to get Americans back to work by plugging wells and restoring the land. Join us for an online roundtable on Tuesday, March 26, at 2:30 p.m. Eastern time with Subcommittee Chair Alan Lowenthal and a panel of experts on how to turn these abandoned wells into an economic and environmental benefit to the country.

362.title: The Growing Threat of Wildlife Disease to Human Health and What We Can Do To Prevent It
362.description: The #Coronavirus was transmitted from animals to humans – and we need to get a head start on making that future viruses don’t make the jump from wildlife. We can’t keep overlooking the role of wildlife in protecting our public health. House Democrats just passed the #HeroesAct to prevent the spread of wildlife-borne diseases to humans. Join us on May 19 at 1:00 p.m. Eastern time for a livestreamed roundtable on the new resources and authorities that wildlife agencies need to protect lives and stop the next pandemic before it starts.

363.title: Coronavirus Impacts to American Fisheries and Seafood Supply Chain
363.description: Responsible social distancing during the #Coronavirus pandemic has closed most restaurants. American fisheries are facing economic setbacks they never could have never prepared for. House Democrats secured $300 million in the #CARESAct to assist fisheries, but that money is still in limbo while the Trump administration struggles to respond. We just passed an additional $100 million in the #HeroesAct that should reach those who need it as soon as possible. Join us on May 18 at 1:00 p.m. Eastern time for a livestreamed roundtable as we hear directly from those affected by the administration’s failures and discuss what’s next.

365.title: Endangered Species Day 2020
365.description:
Since becoming law in the 1970s, the Endangered Species Act has prevented the extinction of 99% of listed species, & animals like bald eagles and humpback whales have fully recovered.
Trump is gutting these protections. This #EndangeredSpeciesDay, join us to #StopExinction.

Joint us to hear from members of Congress and a panel of experts.

We’re working to close the loopholes in our legal system and stop violence against missing and murdered indigenous women.

#MMIW

369.title: Behind the Curtain: The Trump Administration's Fossil Fuel Agenda During the Pandemic
369.description: As the whole country struggles against the #Coronavirus, President Trump and his staff should be protecting our health – but they continue to focus limited resources on helping polluters and slashing environmental protections. We’re hosting a virtual roundtable on Tuesday, May 5, to investigate the administration’s fossil fuel giveaway agenda during the pandemic. Joint us to hear from members of Congress and a panel of experts. Watch live here at 1 p.m. Eastern time.

370.title: Federal Coronavirus Response in U.S. Territories
370.description:
The #Coronavirus is posing a unique threat to U.S. territories. Chair Raul M. Grijava and Rep. Sablan and Rep. San Nicolas are hosting a livestreamed roundtable on Wednesday, April 29, on relief for the territories and why abandoning them now would be a terrible mistake.
 
Americans in Puerto Rico are living in one of the nation’s strictest lockdowns and have very limited access to testing. Hundreds of sick Navy sailors are being treated in Guam.  The islands are uniquely vulnerable because of decades of federal economic neglect and a lack of health care infrastructure. The spread of #Coronavirus is overwhelming territorial communities, and Congress needs to send help. Watch live here at 6 p.m. Eastern.

371.title: Environmental Justice Impacts from Coronavirus Health & Economic Crises
371.description: Air and water pollution disproportionately hurt people of color. Decades of building waste incinerators, chemical refineries and other heavily polluting industries in minority neighborhoods – and ignoring the needs of rural minority communities – have condemned generations to higher rates of sickness and poverty. The #Coronavirus pandemic is aggravating these disparities. Join us for a livestreamed roundtable in partnership with Congressman Donald A. McEachin, Rep. Alan Lowenthal and Rep. Deb Haaland this Tuesday, April 28, at 1 p.m. Eastern time as we hear from #EnviroJusticeNow leaders on how #Coronavirus is laying bare our country’s inequalities – and what we can do to fix them.

373.title: Dr. Steven Emerman Testimony - Resolution Copper Mining at Oak Flat
373.description: Building a copper mine in the middle of Native sacred land is a profound environmental injustice. The Trump administration and Resolution Copper are bulldozing full speed ahead in central Arizona and threatening sites like Apache Leap that will never be repaired if the mine is built. The Subcommittee for Indigenous Peoples of the United States held an oversight hearing on Thursday, March 12, at 9 a.m. Eastern to get to the bottom of who this project would really benefit, and who it would hurt.

384.title: Introducing the Environmental Justice for All Act
384.description:
Washington, D.C. – Chair Raúl M. Grijalva (D-Ariz.) and Rep. A. Donald McEachin (D-Va.) introduced their landmark Environmental Justice for All Act at a press conference today on Capitol Hill. The event marked the culmination of a yearlong process with advocates and stakeholders in which Members of Congress met with and gathered feedback from the public and the environmental justice community to craft the legislation.

“Justice and equity must be at the center of environmental and conservation policy,” Chair Grijalva said. “For too long, low-income communities, tribal and indigenous communities, and communities of color have been shut out of the decision-making process and left without the tools to fight back when big corporations set up shop in their back yards. We cannot turn a blind eye as communities suffer. Today we’re turning the page to give the power back to impacted communities, where it should have been all along. I’m grateful for the community members who trusted us and engaged with us throughout this process, and for my partner Congressman McEachin. The journey for justice is long, and our bill is a big step forward to ensure environmental justice for all.”

“In far too many American communities, the fundamental rights to clean air, pure water, and an environment free of toxic pollution remain unrealized,” Rep. McEachin said. “With today’s introduction of the Environmental Justice for All Act, we are taking meaningful action toward ameliorating these wrongs and empowering the low-income communities, communities of color, and Tribal and indigenous communities disproportionately affected by environmental injustice to fiercely participate in the decision-making processes impacting their well-being. I am proud to have worked alongside Chair Grijalva and environmental justice communities across our country on this comprehensive bill and look forward to continuing our work to ensure that our society becomes healthy and sustainable for all.”

A livestream of the press conference can be viewed at http://bit.ly/3cfnv2w and photos can be viewed at http://bit.ly/397uTuC. 

Original cosponsors of the Environmental Justice for All Act include Committee Vice-Chair Deb Haaland (D-N.M.), Rep. Alan Lowenthal (D-Calif.), Chair of the Subcommittee on Energy and Mineral Resources, Rep. Jesús G. ‘Chuy’ Garcia (D-Ill.), Rep. Joseph P. Kennedy III (D-Mass.), Rep. Nanette Diaz Barragan (D-Calif.), Rep. Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.), Rep. Adriano Espaillat (D-N.Y.), Rep. Barbara Lee (D-Calif.), Rep. Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), Rep. Yvette D. Clarke (D-N.Y.), Rep. Judy Chu (D-Calif.), Rep. Joe Neguse (D-Colo.), Rep. Janice D. Schakowsky (D-Ill.), Rep. Grace Meng (D-N.Y.), Rep. Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.), Rep. Donald S. Beyer, Jr. (D-Va.), Rep. Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), and Rep. Pramila Jayapal (D-Wash.).

The newly introduced legislation enjoys enthusiastic support from environmental justice groups.

snippet.title: Introducing the Environmental Justice for All Act
snippet.description:
Washington, D.C. – Chair Raúl M. Grijalva (D-Ariz.) and Rep. A. Donald McEachin (D-Va.) introduced their landmark Environmental Justice for All Act at a press conference today on Capitol Hill. The event marked the culmination of a yearlong process with advocates and stakeholders in which Members of Congress met with and gathered feedback from the public and the environmental justice community to craft the legislation.

“Justice and equity must be at the center of environmental and conservation policy,” Chair Grijalva said. “For too long, low-income communities, tribal and indigenous communities, and communities of color have been shut out of the decision-making process and left without the tools to fight back when big corporations set up shop in their back yards. We cannot turn a blind eye as communities suffer. Today we’re turning the page to give the power back to impacted communities, where it should have been all along. I’m grateful for the community members who trusted us and engaged with us throughout this process, and for my partner Congressman McEachin. The journey for justice is long, and our bill is a big step forward to ensure environmental justice for all.”

“In far too many American communities, the fundamental rights to clean air, pure water, and an environment free of toxic pollution remain unrealized,” Rep. McEachin said. “With today’s introduction of the Environmental Justice for All Act, we are taking meaningful action toward ameliorating these wrongs and empowering the low-income communities, communities of color, and Tribal and indigenous communities disproportionately affected by environmental injustice to fiercely participate in the decision-making processes impacting their well-being. I am proud to have worked alongside Chair Grijalva and environmental justice communities across our country on this comprehensive bill and look forward to continuing our work to ensure that our society becomes healthy and sustainable for all.”

A livestream of the press conference can be viewed at http://bit.ly/3cfnv2w and photos can be viewed at http://bit.ly/397uTuC.

388.title: Introducing the Environmental Justice for All Act
388.description:
Following Year-Long Collaborative Effort, Chair Grijalva and Rep. McEachin Introducing Landmark Environmental Justice Bill at Thursday Press Conference
Washington, D.C. – Chair Raúl M. Grijalva (D-Ariz.) and Rep. A. Donald McEachin (D-Va.) will introduce their landmark Environmental Justice for All Act at a press conference this Thursday at 10:00 a.m. Eastern time in Longworth 1334 in Washington, D.C. The event, part of a yearlong process with advocates and stakeholders, will be livestreamed at http://facebook.com/nrdems. 

Among other key features, the bill creates a Federal Energy Transition Economic Development Assistance Fund – paid for by new fees on oil, gas and coal companies – to support communities and workers as they transition away from greenhouse gas-dependent economies. The bill expands legal rights for underserved communities and creates new federal grants and program authority to address environmental racism and disparate impacts nationwide.

Grijalva and McEachin released a discussion draft version of the bill in November 2019, which subsequently served as the basis for months of public input and recommendations through an innovative online comment tool called POPVOX. The introduction of the final bill opens a new phase of the lawmakers’ ongoing project to revitalize environmental justice in federal policy. 

The lawmakers held a daylong convening on environmental justice at the U.S. Capitol on June 26, 2019, and continue to host regular discussions of the Environmental Justice Working Group, an alliance of stakeholders that helped craft the Environmental Justice for All Act from its inception. In addition to opening the draft bill to online comments, the authors used outside recommendations to shape the statement of principles on which the bill was ultimately based.

The bill includes issues in the Natural Resources Committee’s jurisdiction, including an update of the National Environmental Policy Act, and Grijalva intends to hold a hearing this year.

When: Thursday, Feb. 27, at 10:00 a.m. Eastern time

Where: 1334 Longworth House Office Building (livestreamed at http://facebook.com/nrdems)

Speakers

Chair Grijalva
Rep. McEachin
Angelo Logan, Moving Forward Network
Taysha DeVaughan, Alliance for Appalachia
Juan Parras, Texas Environmental Justice Advocacy Services
Kim Gaddy, Clean Water Action of New Jersey

396.title: Witness Testimony Highlights from Full Committee Hearing On Climate Change Bills
396.description:
On Wednesday, February 26, 2020 at 10:00 a.m., in Room 1324 Longworth House Office Building, the Committee on Natural Resources held a legislative hearing on the following bills:


H.R. 5435 (Rep. Grijalva), To require the Secretary of the Interior and the Chief of the United States Forest Service to meet certain targets for the reduction of the emission of greenhouse gases, and for other purposes. “American Public Lands and Waters Climate Solution Act of 2019.”
H.R. 5859 (Rep. Westerman), To establish forest management, reforestation, and utilization practices which lead to the sequestration of greenhouse gases, and for other purposes. “Trillion Trees Act.”

412.title: Chair Grijalva, Committee Democrats to Introduce Landmark Climate Change Legislation
412.description:
Washington D.C. – Chair Raúl M. Grijalva (D-Ariz.) and several members of the Natural Resources Committee led a press conference at 12:00 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday, Dec. 17, to unveil their flagship legislation to fight the climate crisis. Members will discuss the legislation’s importance and describe the path it provides to end our public lands’ and waters’ contribution to climate change by 2040.

The landmark bill – authored by Grijalva and cosponsored by a team of Committee members – is the culmination of a year of hearings, roundtables, public forums and other public outreach efforts to learn more about how best to tackle climate change. Since taking the House majority, Natural Resources Committee Democrats have spent much of the past year tackling climate change from every angle.

According to the U.S. Geological Survey, climate-harming emissions from public lands account for nearly a quarter of the U.S. total. The new bill seeks to reduce that figure while simultaneously promoting positive climate actions so that the total net contribution of public lands to greenhouse gas emissions is zero by 2040.

In February, the Committee kicked off a historic month of climate change hearings to hear from impacted communities, launched an online platform to hear from the American people about how climate change has impacted them, and held 22 hearings in 2019 focused on climate change to hear from experts, community members, Indian Country, scientists, and advocates.

The feedback gathered through these efforts has consistently underscored the urgent need to limit climate pollution as soon as possible, and to help impacted communities adapt quickly.

The bill is endorsed by multiple stakeholders and public interest advocacy groups, who will provide remarks at the press conference.

413.title: Press Conference on Moving the Bureau of Land Management to Grand Junction, CO
413.description: Chair Raúl M. Grijalva (D-Ariz.) and Rep. Deb Haaland (D-N.M.), the chairwoman of the Subcommittee on National Parks, Forests, and Public Lands, led a press conference at 9:00 a.m. Eastern time on Wednesday morning, December 11th, 2019 at the U.S. Capitol to discuss the Trump administration’s forced move of hundreds of Bureau of Land Management (BLM) employees to Grand Junction, Colo., and elsewhere across the West. Former BLM Director Bob Abbey and former BLM Deputy Director Henri Bisson will speak at the event to share their perspectives on the move’s potential implications and to encourage the administration to give impacted employees the support and consideration they have so far been denied.

441.title: Subcommittee for Indigenous Peoples of the United States Legislative Hearing EventID=109959
441.description: Our Subcommittee for Indigenous Peoples of the United States is meeting this Thursday, Sept. 19, for a legislative hearing on 4 bills that improve health care access for Native American veterans and increase land rights for conservation and research purposes. Additionally, Ben Ray Luján’s STOP Act prohibits exporting culturally sacred Native American objects and increases penalties for stealing and illegally trafficking tribal cultural patrimony. Watch here at 2:00 p.m. Eastern to hear testimony and follow the debate live.

451.title: Natural Resources Pride Forum
451.description:
On July 24th, 2019 at 1:30 pm in room 1334 of the Longworth House Office Building, the House Committee on Natural Resources will host an LGBTQ Pride forum. The National Parks Service’s theme for July is “Telling All Americans’ Stories”, but in truth, not all Americans’ stories are portrayed equally. The Natural Resources Committee will continue pride month into July by hosting a conversation between members and LGBTQ advocates to raise awareness and learn how the Committee may elevate LGBTQ stories and increase representation throughout America’s public lands.


Some of the issues we will explore in-depth include:
- The importance and process of finding, interpreting, and sharing LGBTQ history
- Barriers to access for the outdoors for the LGBTQ community
- Special LGBTQ connections to the outdoors
- Opportunities for boosting representation and inclusion of the LGBTQ community in connection with public lands and waters


Guest Panelists:
 
Elyse Rylander- Founder and Director, Out There Adventures,
 
Chad Lord- National Parks Conservation Association, Stonewall designation
 
Sue Ferentinos- author of Interpreting LGBT History at Museums and Historic Sites
 
Laura Esquivel- Hispanic Federation, former Senior Vice president of the Gay and Lesbian Victory Fund and Gay and Lesbian Leadership Institute

464.title: Environmental Justice Convening: Afternoon Session
464.description: Chair Raul Grijalva and Rep. A. Donald McEachin are hosting an environmental justice summit at the U.S. Capitol Visitor Center Auditorium on June 26. This all-day event will bring hundreds of participants from across the country to discuss long-standing injustices and areas of collaboration between advocates and policymakers. Throughout the day, policymakers and a broad range of organizations and individuals will participate in panel discussions on a variety of topics, including the history and context of the environmental justice movement and environmental justice organizations’ current challenges and policy priorities. This first-of-its-kind convening is designed to mobilize support for environmental justice and spur legislative action.

465.title: Water, Oceans and Wildlife Subcommittee Hearing EventID=109713
465.description: Many Native communities across the country lack access to reliable water sources. The federal government has a trust responsibility to ensure access to water for federally recognized tribes, and we’re working to pass legislation to address this injustice. Tribal communities should have clean drinking water. On Wednesday, June 26, at 2:00 p.m. Eastern time, our Water, Oceans and Wildlife Subcommittee meets to discuss H.R. 644, H.R. 2459, and H.R. 3292 to develop water infrastructure that protects vital water rights for tribes.

Throughout the day, policymakers and a broad range of organizations and individuals will participate in panel discussions on a variety of topics, including the history and context of the environmental justice movement and environmental justice organizations’ current challenges and policy priorities. This first-of-its-kind convening is designed to mobilize support for environmental justice and spur legislative action.

467.title: Full Committee Markup EventID=109725
467.description:
We’re hosting a markup to push two important bills this Wednesday.
1. Congressman Joe Neguse introduced the #CoreAct to protect approximately 400,000 thousand acres of land in Colorado - establishing new wilderness areas and safeguarding existing outdoor recreation opportunities to boost the economy for future generations.
2. Rep. Rob Bishop’s maintained bill aims to address the shortfall left by Republican-controlled Congresses that failed to fund billions in public lands maintenance costs. #FixOurParks. 
Watch live at 10:00 a.m. Eastern time on Wednesday, June 26, as we come together to move these bills through Committee and one step closer to becoming law.

474.title: Congressional Leaders Protecting Chaco Canyon From Oil and Gas Drilling
474.description: Rep. Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) is leading the fight to protect Chaco Culture National Historical Park from destructive oil and gas drilling. His Chaco Cultural Heritage Area Protection Act (H.R. 2181), supported by leaders like Chair Raúl M. Grijalva (D-Ariz.) and Vice Chair Deb Haaland (D-N.M.), creates a buffer around the park and protects sacred Native American sites for the long term. This effort is bigger than any one person; please join us and spread the word.

478.title: Press Conference on Funding the Land and Water Conservation Fund
478.description: On June 12, Rep. Jeff Van Drew (D-N.J.) introduced a bill to guarantee full funding of the Land and Water Conservation Fund, which protects public land all over the country. LWCF is funded by a royalty on offshore oil and gas drilling, and if we don't spend it, less land is protected. Join us in fighting for a greener future that benefits everyone.

514.title: Press Conference on New Report on Federal Consultation of Tribes
514.description: Chair Raúl Grijalva (D-Ariz.), Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D. (D-Calif.), and Chairperson Aaron Payment host a press conference to announce the release of a new GAO report entitled “Tribal Consultation: Additional Federal Actions Needed for Infrastructure Projects.” The report is the first-ever comprehensive review of 21 federal agencies’ tribal consultation processes for the development and implementation of federal infrastructure projects. The report found that many federal agencies lack the necessary policies and implementation mechanisms to consult tribes impacted by federal infrastructure projects. May 1, 2019.

530.title: Grijalva Statement
530.description: After a 19-year drought, the seven Colorado River Basin states came together to address water shortages with the new Colorado River Drought Contingency Plan. The Subcommittee on Water, Oceans and Wildlife heard from these states as they present the plan and explain how water will be shared. Chairman Grijalva will introduce a bill with support from all 7 Colorado River Basin states & regional tribes that authorizes the Colorado River Drought Contingency Plan. It will preserve water for the Southwest and the 40 million Americans who live there.

601.title: Climate Change: The Impacts and the Need to Act
601.description:
Under Chair @RepRaulGrijalva’s leadership, the Natural Resources Committee is hosting the first House hearing on #climatechange in more than eight years. Watch live this Wednesday, February 6, at 10 a.m. Eastern time. 

Record-setting hurricanes, floods, wildfires and droughts don’t just happen – they’re intensifying because of #ClimateChange. Join us as we take the first step to #ActOnClimate and break eighty years of Republican silence and denial. The American people deserve answers and demand action.

635.title: Hearing on SHARE Act to Deregulate Gun Silencers and Armor Piercing Bullets Sept  12 2017
635.description:
On Sept. 12, 2017, the Natural Resources Committee held a hearing on the SHARE Act by Rep. Jeff Duncan (R-S.C.), which deregulates gun silencers and makes it harder to regulate armor-piercing bullets, among other harmful measures. The bill was supposed to be about helping sportsmen access public lands. The hearing featured testimony by 25-year ATF veteran David Chipman that these kinds of giveaways to the National Rifle Association hurt public safety and bring no public benefit, although they may increase sales for gun and silencer manufacturers.

Learn more at http://democrats-naturalresources.house.gov.

649.title: The Antiquities Act
649.description: The Antiquities Act authorizes the president to designate national monuments on existing federal land. Since its enactment in 1906, it has been used to protect some of our nation's most iconic historical landmarks and natural landscapes, from the Grand Canyon in Arizona to the Stonewall Inn in New York City. Despite this historic function, Republicans are eager to dismantle and restrict the Antiquities Act. Check out the video to learn more.
